title: Verilog-A, Mixed-Signal and Integration
intro: Beyond the built-in devices: Verilog-A models compiled to .osdi files, digital and mixed-signal simulation with XSPICE, co-simulation with Verilog and VHDL, ngspice as a library inside other programs, and the specialist features most users never meet.

items: Verilog-A Models and OSDI: OpenVAF, compiling .va files, loading .osdi files, N instances, model parameters, operating-point values, noise, and the industry compact models.
Writing Verilog-A for ngspice: the language subset OpenVAF accepts, with a tested diode, a self-heating resistor and behavioural blocks, and what does not work.

XSPICE Digital and Mixed-Signal Simulation: event-driven digital models, bridges between analog and digital nodes, state machines, digital output, PSpice digital libraries and writing your own code models.
Co-Simulation with Verilog and VHDL: d_cosim with Verilator, Icarus Verilog and GHDL.
Shared Library and Python: libngspice, its C API, driving it from Python with ctypes, PySpice and friends, and KiCad and Xschem integration.
Specialist Features: CIDER device simulation, transmission lines, radiation (SEE) pulses, sound files, snapshots, tclspice and other rarely used corners.
Quick Reference: elements, analyses, options and commands on one page.
